EU Investigates von der Leyen Over Zelensky Chat — The European ombudsman has opened an investigation into European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen’s handling of a private group chat involving Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and several European leaders. The inquiry will examine whether the Commission breached EU transparency rules by refusing public access to the messages.

SBU, FBI Uncover Russian Cyber Campaign Targeting Officials — On Thursday, Ukraine’s Security Service (SBU) and the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) said they uncovered a coordinated Russian cyber campaign targeting the messaging accounts of officials, military personnel, politicians, and activists in Ukraine, Europe, and the US. The agencies warned that Russian hackers are also attempting to compromise the personal accounts of ordinary Ukrainians.

Lukashenko Resists Kremlin Pressure to Open New Front Against Ukraine — ISW says the Kremlin is pressuring Lukashenko to deepen Belarus’s role in Russia’s war, including allowing drone launches and opening a new pressure front against Ukraine. However, Minsk appears to be resisting, as shown by the shutdown of drone-guiding repeaters near the border after Zelensky’s ultimatum. Russia also continues rejection of compromise peace talks and worsening domestic fuel shortages caused by Ukrainian stri

Ukraine Recovery Conference Opens In Gdańsk Under Shadow Of Kyiv-Warsaw Dispute — EU leaders, investors, and officials gather in Gdańsk for the Ukraine Recovery Conference, aimed at mobilizing billions for reconstruction and defense investments. But the summit is overshadowed by a Kyiv–Warsaw political dispute that has strained relations and raised questions over regional unity despite continued Polish support for Ukraine.

Polish Deep-Strike Drone With 1,000-km Range Tested Near Kyiv — A Polish-made deep-strike drone capable of flying up to 1,000 kilometers has been tested near Kyiv and received positive feedback from Ukrainian operators. The Striker UAV can carry up to 60 kg of explosives and is designed to hit targets deep behind enemy lines.
CARTOON: Lukashenko Feels the Squeeze and Dithers — Serhiy Kolyada’s ironic take on the latest international events.

Ukraine War: Should Europe Mediate? — European commentators are divided over whether growing pressure on Russia—through Ukraine’s strikes and signs of economic strain—creates an opening for peace negotiations. Some argue Europe should take a more active diplomatic role, while others warn that EU divisions, Putin’s continued belief in victory, and concerns over Russian instability could undermine meaningful talks.

Ukrainian Drones Hit Russian Oil Depot in Krasnodar Region for Second Time in 10 Days — A reported Ukrainian drone attack triggered a fire at Russia’s Poltavskaya oil depot overnight, with monitoring channels saying three fuel tanks were ablaze and authorities closing nearby roads.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, June 24, 2026 — Latest from the Institute for the Study of War.

Russia Must ‘Feel the War It Started,’ Zelensky Says, Ordering Preemptive Strikes on Russian Sites — President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine’s strikes on Russian military, energy and logistics targets are a response to Moscow’s attacks on Ukrainian cities and villages. He said Ukrainian forces are targeting facilities that sustain Russia’s war effort, including ammunition depots, military production sites, gas and oil facilities, and strategic communication centers.

Trump Calls Zelensky ‘Courageous’ as Rutte Pushes to Keep Ukraine Armed — US President Donald Trump said President Volodymyr Zelensky is “doing pretty well” and “holding his own” against Russia during an Oval Office meeting with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, as Kyiv presses allies for more air defense, interceptors and long-range capabilities.

Venezuela Declares State of Emergency After Two Powerful Earthquakes — Venezuela declared a state of emergency after two powerful earthquakes struck the same area on Wednesday evening. The 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude quakes caused panic in Caracas, damaged buildings and prompted officials to cut gas supplies to several structures as a precaution.

Explosions Reported Across Occupied Crimea Amid Drone Attack — Occupied Crimea came under a reported drone attack in the early hours of Thursday, with explosions heard near Sevastopol, Simferopol, Saki and the Balaklava Thermal Power Plant. Monitoring channels reported active Russian air defenses, while the Atesh partisan movement claimed the attack affected the entire peninsula.

Trump Says Zelensky Is ‘Doing Pretty Well’ in War Against Russia — US President Donald Trump praised Volodymyr Zelensky’s wartime leadership, saying the Ukrainian president is “doing pretty well” and “holding his own” against Russian forces. The remarks came after their recent G7 meeting in France, where leaders agreed to intensify pressure on Moscow.

Russian Drone Attack on Sumy Injures Child, Damages Homes and Cars — Russian drones struck Sumy on Wednesday evening, injuring a 13-year-old boy and causing damage to residential areas, vehicles and an industrial facility. Ukrainian air defenses intercepted a number of drones before they reached the city, according to regional authorities.

US State Department Says Ukraine Is Currently Winning the War — Jeremy Levin, a senior US State Department authority, said in Gdansk that Ukraine is now in a phase where it is winning the war, stating Kyiv has “turned the situation around” and seized battlefield initiative. According to him, Ukrainian forces are reversing earlier patterns of the conflict, shifting to offensive while Russian troops wait for winter. He also highlighted Ukrainian strikes on Russian infrastructure, while signaling t

Zelensky: Russia Turns Moscow Into ‘Fortress’ With S-400, S-500, Pantsir Air Defense — President Volodymyr Zelensky says Russia has concentrated “hundreds of launchers” of S-400, S-500 and Pantsir air defense systems around Moscow, describing the capital as a heavily protected “fortress.” Meanwhile, additional launchers were pulled from other regions, he says, to create strong defenses near leadership-linked areas, such as Valdai. Zelensky frames this as a sign that Russia prioritizes shielding

Russia Turns to India for Gasoline as Drone Strikes Cut Output by 25% — Russia is preparing tax amendments to subsidize gasoline imports from India as domestic fuel production falls sharply following repeated Ukrainian drone attacks on critical infrastructure. Reportedly, Russia’s output has dropped by around 25%, with the county now facing a deficit equal to 20% of internal demand. Existing imports from Belarus cover only a fraction of the shortfall, prompting Moscow to seek supplies from its l

IMF Clears Ukraine's First Review Under Fire. What Comes Next? — The IMF pushed through Ukraine’s first program review even as Russian strikes hit Kyiv during the mission’s visit. It retreated again on tax conditions after only one of four required bills cleared parliament. Sources close to the talks describe the IMF as furious but flexible – a tension that will face its next test in September, when the Fund and Ukraine must agree on the size of the 2027 financing gap.

Zelensky: Belarus Halted Retransmitters for Russian Shahed Drones — President Volodymyr Zelensky said Belarus has stopped using retransmitters that Russia relied on to guide Shahed drones toward targets in Ukraine. Citing reports from Ukraine’s commander-in-chief and intelligence services, he said the systems ceased operating on Belarusian territory on Monday, just days after he issued a public ultimatum to Belarusian leader Alexander Lukashenko to remove them. No official comments came from Min

Denmark to Supply Ukraine With 15,000 Long-Range Artillery Rounds — Minister of Defense Mykhailo Fedorov announced that Denmark will transfer 15,000 long-range artillery rounds after Kyiv requested Copenhagen to shift support away from short-range systems toward long-range solutions, deemed more effective. Ukrainian officials say their priorities remain air defense, long-range artillery and drones, stating that such ammunition is vital as drone “kill zones” expand along the front. Part of the ne

Fuel Sales Restricted in 22 Russian Regions — Fuel sale restrictions have been introduced in 22 Russian regions, affecting roughly one-quarter of the country’s federal subjects, according to Russian media reports. Regional authorities have blamed supply disruptions, rising prices and increased demand, while the restrictions come amid ongoing Ukrainian strikes targeting Russia’s oil refining sector.

Ukraine Calls on Allies to Expand Support for Air Defense, Drones and Artillery — Ukraine is expanding its technological defense capabilities while calling for greater international support in air defense, drone and missile production, and long-range artillery. Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov outlined these priorities at the RUSI Land Warfare Conference in London, citing battlefield progress amid ongoing challenges. Greater allied cooperation and funding, he said, are essential to sustaining t

Russian Strike Hits Beach in Zaporizhzhia, Injures 6, Including 3 Children — Russian forces struck a beach in Zaporizhzhia on Wednesday, injuring 6 people, including 3 children, regional authorities said. The attack came amid heightened threats from drone strikes in the area, following a series of recent Russian strikes on civilian infrastructure throughout the city.

Zelensky Says Ukraine Blew Up 60,000 Tons of Ammo Near St. Petersburg — Zelensky on Wednesday said Ukrainian long-range strikes destroyed over 60,000 tons of ammunition at a Baltic Fleet arsenal near St. Petersburg, based on a report from the HUR chief. Zelensky also said Ukraine hit Russian electronics and defense production facilities and obtained documents showing Russia shifting air defenses to protect Moscow and the Kerch Bridge, weakening other regions.

Four Ukrainian Sailors Returned From Iran — Four Ukrainian sailors who were aboard the Epimonidas container ship when it was detained by Iranian forces in April have returned home, Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry said. Ukrainian diplomats worked with the sailors’ families, the Greek shipowner and international partners to secure their return from Iran.

Russian Military Recruitment Falls Across Country — The flow of new recruits into Russia’s military has fallen significantly across the country, according to a report published by independent outlet Verstka on Wednesday. Sources cited by the publication said recruitment targets are becoming harder to meet, along with difficult quotas, despite rising financial incentives.

Moscow Refinery Knocked Offline Until 2027 After Drone Strikes – Sources Say — Moscow’s largest fuel refinery is expected to remain offline until early 2027 after repeated Ukrainian drone strikes, two industry sources say. The attacks damaged key processing units at the Gazprom Neft-owned plant, which supplies most of the capital’s fuel.

Russia Says Nuclear Weapons the ‘Only’ Guarantee Against Global War — The Kremlin warned that nuclear weapons remain the “only” safeguard against global war as Dmitry Peskov said the international security system is “eroding.” His remarks came after the New START treaty between Russia and the US expired, ending the last remaining limits on the world’s two largest nuclear arsenals.

Rutte Says Trump Aides Working on Ukraine Peace Plan — NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said senior US officials, including Marco Rubio, Steve Witkoff, and Jared Kushner, are working to secure a peace agreement in Ukraine. Rutte also defended NATO against criticism from Trump, stressing continued European support for US military operations.

Lavrov Rejects Frontline Freeze as Basis for Ukraine Peace Talks — Lavrov rejected a frontline freeze as a basis for Ukraine peace talks, insisting on conditions Moscow considers “reasonable” and accusing Kyiv and the West of derailing past deals. He repeated Russia’s claim that previous negotiations collapsed after the Istanbul talks and Western interference, including former UK PM Boris Johnson’s role.

EXPLAINED: Ukraine Opens EU Talks With Justice System Still Mired in Power Struggle — As Ukraine begins EU accession talks, concerns persist over stalled problems in its judiciary, including cases linked to the “Vovk tapes” and controversial Supreme Court rulings reinstating discredited judges. While reforms have produced results, parts of the system continue to resist change, raising doubts about the effectiveness of alignment with EU standards.

Ukraine Expects Breakthrough in EU Entry, 5 Clusters Set for Mid-July — Ukraine expects all EU accession negotiation clusters to be ready for opening by mid-July, with the deputy prime minister saying the process now depends mainly on coordination among EU member states. Kachka added that no further decisions are required and that Ukraine aims to meet the benchmarks by 2027, with accession potentially possible by 2030. However, Hungary has slowed procedural steps, raising doubts over the timelin

Poland Rejects Mediation in Ukraine Dispute — Poland’s government said it does not require outside mediation to resolve a growing diplomatic dispute with Ukraine. The disagreement, which centers on differing interpretations of historical events during World War II, has led to a series of retaliatory political moves and prompted calls from European officials for de-escalation.

Russian Security Chiefs Push Duma Election Delay — Senior Russian security officials are lobbying Russian leader Putin to postpone September’s State Duma elections. That concerns over economic difficulties, declining support for the ruling United Russia party and recent Ukrainian drone attacks on Moscow have increased discussions about delaying the vote, although elections remain scheduled for Sept. 18-20.

90% of Ukrainians Want History Disputes With Poland Kept Out of Politics – KIIS Poll — A new KIIS poll shows 90% of Ukrainians want historical disputes with Poland kept out of politics and resolved through pragmatic or academic channels. Attitudes toward Poles remain broadly tolerant despite recent fluctuations, while perceptions of OUN-UPA have shifted significantly toward more positive or uncertain views since 2013.

NATO Ground Commander in Europe, Key Figure in Ukraine Support, to Step Down Early Amid Pentagon Shake-Up — Gen. Christopher Donahue, who oversees US Army operations in Europe and support for Ukraine, will step down on July 2, becoming the latest senior officer to leave amid Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s push to thin the ranks of top US military leaders.

Cutting Off Crimea — Ukraine’s “logistical lockdown” aimed at “turning Crimea into an island,” is gaining momentum, with fuel now scarce and many parts of the occupied peninsula plunged into darkness due to strikes against power plants. Kyiv understands that by crippling Crimea they are stabbing the symbolic heart of Putin’s revanchist project.

Mass Drone Raid Hits Orenburg Gas Giant 1,500 km From Ukraine, Russia’s Only Helium Plant Ablaze — Ukraine struck the Orenburg Gas Processing Plant and Russia’s only helium plant, over 1,200 km (746 miles) from the front, causing fires at a key energy complex used in military-linked production. Separately, authorities in the Nizhny Novgorod region reported a drone strike on an industrial facility, with two people killed and two injured. Russia said air defenses downed hundreds of drones nationwi

Rutte Heads to Washington to Calm Trump Ahead of NATO Summit — NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte is meeting U.S. President Donald Trump ahead of the July NATO summit to ease tensions over Iran, European defense spending, and potential U.S. troop reductions in Europe. Rutte aims to preserve alliance unity as concerns grow over Trump’s criticism of NATO, threats to leave the alliance, and demands for greater burden-sharing by European members.

Ukraine Divisions Fade as Visegrád Leaders Reunite After Two-Year Rift — Central Europe’s Visegrád Group has reconvened for its first leaders’ summit in more than two years, seeking to rebuild ties fractured by Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Political shifts in Hungary have revived hopes for closer cooperation on energy, migration and EU policy.

Polish FM Sikorski Warns Putin May Use False-Flag Attack as Pretext for New Strikes — Polish FM warned that Russia may be preparing a staged provocation on its own territory to justify further escalation, comparing it to Nazi Germany’s 1939 Gleiwitz false-flag incident used as a pretext for war. Sikorski’s remarks followed Putin’s claims that NATO and the EU are fabricating a Russian threat to justify militarisation, while Russian officials accused the West of preparing for conflict.

In High-Stakes Bluff, Putin Holds a Losing Hand — Ukraine’s recent battlefield successes do not bode well for the Kremlin leader. Thanks to Europe’s steady financial and military support for Kyiv, Russia is experiencing casualties unprecedented since World War II. Meanwhile, the US waivers in its historic transatlantic commitment.

Ukraine Targets Crimean Supply Lines – Reactions — Ukrainian strikes on supply routes to Russian-occupied Crimea are disrupting fuel deliveries, transport links, and tourism, increasing economic pressure on the peninsula. Commentators argue the campaign weakens Russia’s southern front, could strengthen Ukraine’s position in future negotiations, and highlights Crimea’s strategic importance to President Vladimir Putin’s political legitimacy.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, June 23, 2026 — Latest from the Institute for the Study of War.

Von der Leyen to Visit Azerbaijan and Armenia as EU Pushes the Middle Corridor to Avoid Russia and Iran — European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen is expected to visit Azerbaijan and Armenia as Brussels pushes to strengthen the Middle Corridor – a trade, energy and digital route linking Europe and Asia while bypassing Russia and Iran.

Occupied Sevastopol Left Completely Without Power After Drone Attack — Occupied Sevastopol was left without electricity after a massive overnight drone attack reportedly hit energy infrastructure in Russian-occupied Crimea. Ukrainian monitoring channels said the Balaklava thermal power plant was among the main targets, while explosions were also reported in Bakhchysarai, Kerch and near Mount Ai-Petri.

Ukraine Heads to Gdańsk Recovery Conference in Poland, Seeking Defense, Energy Deals — Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko said she will lead Ukraine’s delegation to the Ukraine Recovery Conference 2026 in Gdańsk, where Kyiv aims to secure concrete agreements on defense capabilities, energy and economic cooperation. The conference, co-hosted by Poland and Ukraine, is expected to focus on reconstruction, investment and sectors heavily damaged by Russia’s war.

North Korea to Equip Navy With Nuclear Weapons, Kim Says — North Korean leader Kim Jong Un said Pyongyang will equip its navy with nuclear weapons and build larger warships, state media reported. Speaking at the commissioning of the Choe Hyon warship, Kim said the program was moving ahead as part of North Korea’s broader nuclear deterrence strategy against the United States and South Korea.

FT: Putin Frustrated as Trump Warms to Ukraine After Drone Successes — The Financial Times reported that Vladimir Putin is growing increasingly frustrated with Donald Trump as Washington continues to support Ukraine instead of pushing Kyiv toward a quick peace deal on Russia’s terms. Ukrainian officials told the FT they see signs of stronger US backing after Ukraine’s recent military gains, including deep-strike drone successes inside Russia.

Hungary Blocks Ukraine, Moldova’s EU Membership Talks — Hungary blocked a key procedural step needed to advance Ukraine and Moldova’s EU membership talks, opposing a joint letter to EU institutions that requires unanimous approval from all 27 member states. The move puts Kyiv’s goal of opening all six negotiating clusters by mid-July in jeopardy, while reflecting Prime Minister Peter Magyar’s cautious stance towards Ukraine’s accession.

Kyiv Smashed, Moscow Burned, Parsing Drone Operations — Russian forces struck Kyiv this week, damaging the historic Pechersk Lavra monastery and several other UNESCO-listed cultural sites. Ukraine responded with its most ambitious drone strike of the war, sending an estimated 250 aircraft against Moscow’s oil refinery infrastructure in a coordinated, multi-wave attack that knocked out roughly half the capital’s petroleum processing capacity. Ukrainian operations also continued systematically tar

Dutch Troops Prepare for Russian-Style NATO Invasion in Germany — Nearly 7,000 Dutch troops are conducting Exercise Fighter Lion in northern Germany through early July, marking it the Netherlands’ largest army exercise in two decades. Soldiers are training with anti-drone tunnels imported from Ukrainian battlefields, operating under constant drone and electronic warfare pressure, alongside practicing complex brigade handoffs, marking the Netherlands one of the first NATO armies to formally and p

South Ossetia’s Leader Quits, Becomes Putin Advisor Instead — South Ossetia’s Moscow-backed president Alan Gagloyev resigned Tuesday to become an advisor to Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin, just weeks after Russia ratified a major integration agreement aligning the breakaway Georgian region’s laws with Moscow’s. Marat Kambolov, a former Russian bureaucrat, was named interim president. Georgia’s ruling party and opposition condemned the deal as de facto annexation, as Russia tightens its political

SBU’s Alpha Unit Marks 32 Years as Zelensky Honors Fallen Soldier — President Volodymyr Zelensky marked the 32nd anniversary of the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) Special Operations Center “Alpha” on Tuesday, presenting state awards to its soldiers and delivering a posthumous distinction to the family of a fallen hero. Zelensky credited Alpha with helping transform the SBU into one of the world’s strongest combat special services since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale invasion in February

Kremlin Insists Economy Is Stable as Budget Deficit Hits $80B — Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov insisted Tuesday that Russia’s macroeconomic stability is “absolutely secured” despite a federal budget shortfall of 2.1 trillion rubles ($28 billion) and surging war-related expenditures. His assurances came as the benchmark MOEX index hit a three-year low, Urals crude fell to around $65 per barrel (roughly $1.55 per gallon or €0.38 per liter), and Ukrainian drone strikes on refineries prompted fuel

Putin Signals Shift on Ukraine Talks, Revives Istanbul Framework — Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin told a government meeting that Moscow is ready for negotiations with Ukraine “on the basis of the agreements” discussed in Istanbul in 2022, claiming those terms once suited Kyiv. He simultaneously described Ukraine’s leadership as a “neo-Nazi” regime, while arguing that battlefield realities favor Russia. Kyiv has insisted any talks must align with Ukraine’s territorial integrity.

Latvia Warns of Russian Missile, Drone Provocations Targeting Baltic States and Poland — Latvian intelligence has warned that Russia may be preparing hybrid provocations against the Baltic states or Poland, including drone or missile incidents aimed at pressuring NATO countries over support for Ukraine. Officials said Moscow is not currently capable of a conventional war with NATO but warned that miscalculations by Russian leadership could increase regional security risks.

‘Biological Terrorism': Russia Burying Anthrax-Infected Livestock — Ukraine’s military intel agency accused Russian forces of improperly disposing of anthrax-infected livestock in the occupied Kherson region, creating risks for civilians, agriculture, and the environment. HUR warned that Moscow could later exploit the situation to accuse Ukraine of using biological weapons.
CARTOON: Ukrainian Drones Liberating Crimea — Serhiy Kolyada’s ironic take on the latest international events.

Defense Ministry Develops Digital Combat Log — Ukraine’s defense ministry is developing a digital combat log to replace paper-based combat records. The system is expected to help military personnel verify combat deployments, calculate combat-related payments, and track service periods that could affect future benefits and deferment eligibility.

‘Too Early to Say Russia Is Losing Africa’: HUR on Moscow’s Post-Wagner Strategy — In an exclusive interview with Kyiv Post, HUR spokesperson said Moscow successfully replaced Wagner with the Defense Ministry-backed Africa Corps and continues to pursue political influence. He also warned that Russian intelligence services are increasingly using disinformation and AI-generated content to fuel instability and advance Kremlin interests in at least 22 African countries.

'No Longer Exists': SSO Says Key Railway Bridge in Crimea Destroyed — Ukraine’s Special Ops on Tuesday reported the destruction of a railway bridge over the North Crimean Canal in occupied Crimea, saying it was used for Russian military logistics. Drones struck the structure in multiple phases, damaging repair equipment after initial hits. The SSO said the operation disrupted Russian transport routes supporting forces in southern Ukraine, though Kyiv Post could not independently verify the foota

Russia Open to Restarting Ukraine Talks, Lavrov Says — Russian Foreign Minister said Moscow is ready to resume negotiations with Ukraine “from where they left off,” while accusing Kyiv of unrealistic demands and the West of losing its role as mediator. Lavrov also claimed the US is increasing pressure on Russia and suggested Ukraine is expanding the conflict’s geography. Lavrov insisted Russia remains prepared to take all necessary measures to defend their interests.

Russian Drone Shrapnel Kills 26-Year-Old Woman on Odesa Beach — On Monday, a Russian drone attack on Ukraine’s Black Sea coast killed a 26-year-old woman and injured a 39-year-old man in Odesa. Officials said emergency services were working at the scene as casualty figures were still being verified.

Russia Says It Is Ready for Dialogue With the EU — Russia is prepared to engage in dialogue with the European Union, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said. The statement comes after weeks of criticism from Moscow directed at Brussels and amid debate within the EU over potential future contacts with the Kremlin.

EXPLAINED: Bridge Destroyed, Blackouts, Fires, Fuel Bans in Crimea — Occupied Crimea is facing growing disruption after repeated Ukrainian strikes on energy, fuel, rail, and military infrastructure. Power outages, fuel rationing, transport restrictions, and heightened security measures suggest Kyiv is intensifying efforts to degrade Russia’s logistical hub on the peninsula. Recent strikes reportedly destroyed a key railway bridge over the North Crimean Canal.

Russia Says US Drifting From Role as ‘Objective Mediator’ in Ukraine War — Russia accused the United States on Tuesday of abandoning its role as an “objective mediator” in efforts to end the war in Ukraine. Moscow said Washington is instead pursuing sanctions pressure, while US-led peace talks remain stalled with little progress in negotiations between Kyiv and Moscow.

Ballistic Missile Strike On Kryvyi Rih Kills 3, Wounds 19 — Russian forces struck Kryvyi Rih with a ballistic missile on June 23, hitting a civilian infrastructure site. At least three people were killed and 19 injured, including five in serious condition. Emergency crews are working at the scene as authorities warn of possible further strikes.

No Place for Smallness When the World Is on Fire: an American Perspective on the Ukrainian-Polish Affair — Mature nations remember history without becoming imprisoned by it. They recognize that former enemies can become trusted allies and that reconciliation is among the greatest achievements of civilization. The American experience can help guide Poland and Ukraine through the current conflict.

Moscow Expands Air Defense Sites in City Parks — Satellite imagery suggests Russian authorities may be preparing another air defense position in western Moscow, trying to strengthen protection of the capital against Ukrainian drone attacks.

Half of Crimea Left Without Power After Overnight Explosions — Monitoring groups reported fires at fuel and transport facilities in and around Kerch, including a petroleum terminal that had already been burning since a previous attack. As a result, the Kerch Bridge was closed throughout the night for more than five hours.

Honduras Plans to Buy Ukrainian Drones for Border Security — Honduras plans to acquire Ukrainian drone technology to support border protection and anti-drug trafficking operations, President Nasry Asfura said after talks with Volodymyr Zelensky. The discussions highlight growing international interest in Ukraine’s battlefield-tested drone capabilities.

Polish President Strips Zelensky of Highest Honor – Reactions — Polish President Karol Nawrocki revoked Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky’s Order of the White Eagle after Ukraine named a military unit after the UPA, a controversial WWII-era nationalist force. Reactions were divided: some viewed the move as a justified response, while others called it politically motivated and harmful to Polish-Ukrainian relations amid Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine.

Ukraine to Spend Record $98 Billion on Defense in 2026 After Zelensky Signs Budget Increase — Ukraine will spend a record $98 billion on defense in 2026 after President Volodymyr Zelensky signed a major budget increase. Backed by EU loans, the funds will boost weapons procurement and troop pay, sharply narrowing the spending gap with Russia amid continued war pressures.

Ukraine Creates Multiple Risk Points Now for Putin — Tim Ash argues that the war in Ukraine is entering a more confident and strategically advantageous phase for Kyiv, driven by advances in drone warfare, expanding European financing, and Ukraine’s growing ability to scale domestic defense production. He says Ukraine is increasingly taking the fight deep into Russia while tightening pressure on Crimea and Belarus, potentially reshaping Moscow’s strategic calculations.

Trump Says GM, Ford to Shift Factories to Missile Production — President Donald Trump said General Motors and Ford will repurpose factory capacity to help produce Patriot and Tomahawk missiles, as Washington ramps up weapons manufacturing amid concerns over dwindling US munitions stockpiles and explores licensed missile production in Europe and Ukraine.

Warsaw Receives Order of the White Eagle Back From Zelensky, Sends to Special Archive — Polish officials on Monday said Zelensky returned the Order of the White Eagle by mail and that the decoration will now be placed in a special presidential archive. The move follows President Karol Nawrocki’s decision to revoke the award, a step that sparked criticism from Kyiv.

Russia Revises History Textbooks to Include North Koreans Fighting in Ukraine — Russian officials said updated history textbooks for high school students will include information about battles involving North Korean troops in Russia’s Kursk region, as well as drone warfare and battlefield tactics used in the conflict.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, June 22, 2026 — Latest from the Institute for the Study of War.

UK Tells Russia at UN: ‘Enough Is Enough’ After Latest Mass Strikes on Ukraine — The UK condemned Russia’s latest mass strikes on Ukrainian cities at the UN Security Council, saying the June 14-15 attack killed at least 11 civilians, and involved 611 drones and 70 missiles, including 40 ballistic and hypersonic missiles. UK envoy James Kariuki accused Moscow of a pattern of “destruction, then denial, then disinformation,” saying attacks on sites such as Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra, Mystetskyi Arsenal an

Russian Overnight Strikes Wound Six Across Ukraine — Russian overnight strikes wounded at least six people across Ukraine, including two elderly people in Zaporizhzhia, three people in Sumy, and one woman in Kharkiv. Kyiv authorities issued an air raid alert early Tuesday and urged residents to seek shelter, while Zaporizhzhia officials reported damage to homes, a service station and a gas station.

‘You Will Never Hold Occupied Lands’: Ukraine Warns Russia at UN to ‘Get Out Before It’s Too Late’ — Ukraine’s UN envoy Andrii Melnyk delivered a forceful address to the Security Council, accusing Russia of deliberate attacks on civilians, children and cultural heritage. He said Putin had joined the “darkest figures of modern history” after the strike on the Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra, defended Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries as legitimate military targets, and warned Moscow it would never

‘Time Is Not on Moscow’s Side’: US Warns Russia at UN as Its Casualties Hit 40,000 a Month — The US told the UN Security Council that “time is not on Moscow’s side,” urging Russia to make a deal as it suffers an estimated 40,000 casualties a month, faces economic strain and struggles to keep pace with Ukraine’s battlefield innovation. The warning came as UN officials reported that May was the deadliest month for Ukrainian civilians since April 2022.

Zelensky Thanks Starmer for Ukraine Support After UK PM Announces Resignation — Zelensky thanked Keir Starmer after the UK prime minister announced his resignation, praising his support for Ukraine and Britain’s role as one of Kyiv’s strongest allies. Starmer had listed “standing with Ukraine” among his government’s achievements.

Russian Light Aircraft Turns to Car Fuel as Aviation Gasoline Runs Dry — Russian general aviation operators have started testing automobile gasoline in light aircraft as aviation fuel becomes increasingly costly and scarce, with some regions reporting stocks sufficient for only one to one-and-a-half months. The An-2 Operators Association has called for state price regulation, while experts warn controls would deepen the shortage rather than resolve it.
